{{nihongo|'''Shinichi Mochizuki'''|望月 新一|Mochizuki Shin'ichi|extra=born March 29, 1969}} is a Japanese mathematician working in [[number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]]. He is one of the main contributors to [[anabelian geometry]]. His contributions include his solution of the [[Anabelian geometry#Formulation of a conjecture of Grothendieck on curves|Grothendieck conjecture in anabelian geometry]] about hyperbolic curves over number fields. Mochizuki has also worked in [[Hodge–Arakelov theory]] and [[p-adic Teichmüller theory|''p''-adic Teichmüller theory]]. ==Biography==

=== Early life ===
Shinichi Mochizuki was born to parents Kiichi and Anne Mochizuki.<ref>[http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/philly/obituary.aspx?n=leah-p-rauch-edelman&pid=3251930 Leah P. (Edelman) Rauch] Philly.com on Mar. 6, 2005</ref> When he was five years old, Shinichi Mochizuki and his family left Japan to live in the United States. His father was Fellow of the Center for International Affairs and Center for Middle Eastern Studies at [[Harvard University]] (1974–76).<ref>[http://www.us-japan.org/otr/bios/mochizuki.html MOCHIZUKI, Kiichi Dr.] National Association of Japan-America Societies, Inc.</ref> Mochizuki attended [[Phillips Exeter Academy]] and graduated in 1985.<ref name="PWB">{{cite news |url=http://libserv23.princeton.edu/princetonperiodicals/cgi-bin/princetonperiodicals?a=d&d=WeeklyBulletin19880620-01.1.4&e=-------en-20--1--txt-IN-----%23 |title=Seniors address commencement crowd |work=Princeton Weekly Bulletin |volume=77 |page=4 |date=20 June 1988 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130403083550/http://libserv23.princeton.edu/princetonperiodicals/cgi-bin/princetonperiodicals?a=d&d=WeeklyBulletin19880620-01.1.4&e=-------en-20--1--txt-IN-----%23 |archive-date=3 April 2013 }}</ref> 

Mochizuki entered [[Princeton University]] as an undergraduate student at the age of 16 and graduated as [[salutatorian]] with an A.B. in mathematics in 1988.<ref name="PWB" /> He completed his senior thesis, titled "Curves and their deformations," under the supervision of [[Gerd Faltings]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mochizuki |first=Shinichi |url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/9941316513506421 |title=Curves and their deformations |date=1988 |publisher=Princeton, NJ: Department of Mathematics |language=English}}</ref> 

He remained at Princeton for graduate studies and received his Ph.D. in mathematics in 1992 after completing his doctoral dissertation, titled "The geometry of the compactification of the [[Hurwitz scheme]]," also under the supervision of Faltings.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Mochizuki |first=Shinichi |url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/997156143506421 |title=The geometry of the compactification of the Hurwitz scheme |date=1992 |language=English}}</ref> 

After his graduate studies, Mochizuki spent two years at Harvard University and then in 1994 moved back to Japan to join the [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS) at [[Kyoto University]], and was promoted to professor in 2002.<ref name="cv" />{{sfn|Castelvecchi|2015}}

===Career===
Mochizuki proved [[Anabelian geometry#Formulation of a conjecture of Grothendieck on curves|Grothendieck's conjecture on anabelian geometry]] in 1996. He was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://elib.zib.de/ICM98/B/3/3/|title=International Congress of Mathematicians 1998|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219042054/http://elib.zib.de/ICM98/B/3/3/|archive-date=2015-12-19}}</ref> In 2000–2008, he discovered several new theories including the theory of [[frobenioid]]s, mono-anabelian geometry and the etale theta theory for line bundles over tempered covers of the [[Tate curve]].

On August 30, 2012,  Mochizuki released four preprints, whose total size was about 500 pages, that developed [[inter-universal Teichmüller theory]] and applied it in an attempt to prove several very famous problems in [[Diophantine geometry]].<ref>[http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Inter-universal%20Teichmuller%20Theory%20IV.pdf Inter-universal Teichmüller theory IV: log-volume computations and set-theoretic foundations], Shinichi Mochizuki, August 2012</ref> These include the strong [[Szpiro conjecture]], the hyperbolic [[Vojta conjecture]] and the [[abc conjecture|''abc'' conjecture]] over every number field.  In September 2018, Mochizuki posted a report on his work by [[Peter Scholze]] and [[Jakob Stix]], which asserted that the third preprint contains an irreparable flaw; he also posted several documents containing his rebuttal of their criticism.<ref name="klarreich">
{{cite magazine |url= https://www.quantamagazine.org/titans-of-mathematics-clash-over-epic-proof-of-abc-conjecture-20180920/ |title=Titans of Mathematics Clash Over Epic Proof of ABC Conjecture
 |magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]] |date=September 20, 2018|first=Erica|last=Klarreich|author-link=Erica Klarreich}}
</ref>  The majority of number theorists have found Mochizuki's preprints very difficult to follow and have not accepted the conjectures as settled, although there are a few prominent exceptions, including Go Yamashita, [[Ivan Fesenko]], and Yuichiro Hoshi, who vouch for the work and have written expositions of the theory.<ref>{{citation|last=Fesenko|first=Ivan|title=Fukugen|author-link=Ivan Fesenko|journal=Inference: International Review of Science|volume=2|issue=3|url=http://inference-review.com/article/fukugen|year=2016|doi=10.37282/991819.16.25|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Roberts|first=David Michael|title=A crisis of identification|journal=Inference: International Review of Science|volume=4|issue=3|url=https://inference-review.com/article/a-crisis-of-identification|year=2019|doi=10.37282/991819.19.2|s2cid=232514600|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

On April 3, 2020, two Japanese mathematicians, [[Masaki Kashiwara]] and Akio Tamagawa, announced that Mochizuki's claimed proof of the ''abc'' conjecture would be published in ''Publications of the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences'', a journal of which Mochizuki is chief editor.<ref name="nature-2020">{{cite journal|first=Davide |last=Castelvecchi|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-020-00998-2 |title=Mathematical proof that rocked number theory will be published |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |date= April 3, 2020 |volume=580|issue=7802|page=177|doi=10.1038/d41586-020-00998-2|pmid=32246118|bibcode=2020Natur.580..177C|s2cid=214786566|access-date= April 4, 2020|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The announcement was received with skepticism by [[Kiran Kedlaya]] and [[Edward Frenkel]], as well as being described by [[Nature (journal)|''Nature'']] as "unlikely to move many researchers over to Mochizuki's camp".<ref name="nature-2020"/> The special issue containing Mochizuki's articles was published on March 5, 2021.<ref name="Mochizuki2021a"/><ref name="Mochizuki2021b"/><ref name="Mochizuki2021c"/><ref name="Mochizuki2021d"/>
